title: API clients: curl, Postman, fetch
idea: An API client lets you send any request you design and read the raw response, so you can test a route before any frontend exists.

analogy.text: Tasting a dish in the kitchen before any guests arrive. You taste exactly what the kitchen made, with no dining room in between.
analogy.breaks: Tasting skips the dining room, so browser-only behavior can still surprise you.

points: A browser's address bar can only send `GET`; other methods need a client.
`curl` runs in the terminal: a command sends a request and prints the response.
Postman is a graphical client: fill in method, URL, headers and body, then send.
`fetch` is built into Node 20, so scripts and tests can call your API.

hero.title: A curl command, part by part

parts.label: Program
parts.note: Sends a request and prints the response. Postman and `fetch` do the same job.

parts.label: Show headers
parts.note: Also prints the response status line and headers, not only the body.

parts.label: Header
parts.note: One request header. Postman: the Headers tab. `fetch`: the `headers` option.

parts.label: Body
parts.note: The body. `-d` alone makes curl send `POST`. Postman: Body tab. `fetch`: `body`.

parts.label: URL
parts.note: The host and the path your server routes on. `$PORT` stands for its port.

code.title: curl in the terminal
code.caption: Three requests from a second terminal, while your server is running.

code.title: The same idea with fetch
code.caption: A stand-in server and `fetch`: send a POST, then ask for a missing route. Step through it, then press Run.

walk.text: A stand-in server: `POST /notes` gets 201, anything else gets 404.
The same parts as the curl command: method, headers and body.
`status` is the number, `ok` is true for 2xx, and `json()` parses the body.
A 404 still resolves: `fetch` rejects on network errors, not on HTTP statuses.
Close the server so the script can exit.

pitfalls: `fetch` rejects on network errors, not on 404 or 500; check `res.ok` yourself.
Send `Content-Type: application/json` with a JSON body; many servers will not parse it otherwise.
In bash and zsh, wrap JSON in single quotes so the shell keeps its double quotes.

quiz.why: `fetch` resolves for any HTTP status. `ok` is false outside 2xx, but the body is still readable.

takeaway: Every client sends the same parts: method, URL, headers and body.

starters: What does `curl -v` show that `curl -i` does not?
